title: US Issues Strongest Public Warning Against Force on Protesters; Washington Pushes May 13 Mediation Talks — FGS Denies
detail: On May 12, 2026, three days before Somalia's constitutional deadline, the United States issued one of its strongest public warnings yet against the use of force on opposition demonstrators. US Chargé d'Affaires Justin Davis told Dawan Africa that violence against peaceful demonstrators was 'never acceptable,' urging Somalia's political leaders to pursue dialogue and compromise. Davis cautioned that continued political instability could harm Somalia's international partnerships, reaffirming US priorities including counterterrorism, governance, economic cooperation, and regional stability. Washington was reported to be pressuring both the federal government and opposition leaders to enter mediation, with talks allegedly scheduled for May 13 inside the heavily fortified Halane compound at Mogadishu's Aden Adde International Airport — the first formal US mediation effort in Somalia's intensifying political dispute. President Mohamud and PM Hamza Abdi Barre were reported as the FGS representatives; the opposition Somali Future Council, including Puntland, would represent the opposition side. However, Somalia's State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Ba'ad denied the reports, saying there were no plans for a US-hosted meeting on May 13. The warning followed a turbulent 48 hours in Mogadishu during which one protester was killed by security forces in Daynile on May 11 (confirmed by the Banadir Regional Police Commissioner), Somali authorities deployed thousands of troops, tanks, and armored vehicles to prevent opposition demonstrations on May 10, and Turkish F-16s overflew the capital in a show of force for the FGS. With Mohamud's term expiring on May 15 and no mediated agreement in place, Somalia's Mogadishu-based foreign partners were visibly alarmed.

media.caption: US Chargé d'Affaires Justin Davis warns against use of force on Somali opposition protesters, May 12, 2026 — Somali Guardian

title: Opposition Announces May 16 Mogadishu Protest — Day After Constitutional Term Expires; Salvation Forum, Future Council Mobilize
detail: Somalia's opposition bloc — including the Somali Future Council (comprising Puntland, Jubbaland, and allied groups) and the Salvation Forum — announced on May 12, 2026 that it would hold a major demonstration in Mogadishu on May 16, the day after President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's constitutional mandate expires on May 15. The announcement represented a significant escalation from the May 10 protest, which had been largely blocked by security force deployments that sealed roads, occupied gathering sites, and placed parts of the capital under effective military lockdown. Opposition leaders declared that the May 16 protest was aimed at rejecting any move by Mohamud to extend his stay in power beyond constitutional limits, reaffirming their position that he would be recognized as 'an ordinary citizen' after May 15. The symbolic selection of May 16 — the day after the deadline — gave the protest maximum political salience: it would either mark the beginning of the post-Mohamud era if he stood down, or the formal beginning of the opposition's rejection of his legitimacy if he did not. Garowe Online reported separately that fear was growing in Mogadishu of a return to Somalia's violent political past. The US warning against force issued hours earlier on May 12 (by Chargé d'Affaires Justin Davis) and the reported push for May 13 mediation talks at Halane were directly linked to preventing a security crackdown on May 16 from triggering the kind of political violence that had repeatedly destabilized Somalia in prior decades. Al-Shabaab, still holding Adan Yabal for Day 23, was assessed by ICG analysts as positioned to exploit any governance breakdown or security vacuum created by the political confrontation.

media.caption: Somalia opposition bloc announces May 16 protest in Mogadishu — the day after Mohamud's constitutional term expires — Garowe Online
